💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that is it time to give your hairstyle and scalp a breath of fresh air?
  • It has been revealed that by significantly reducing hair volume, undercuts allow for improved air circulation around the scalp.
  • Whether you’re battling irritation or want to give your “do” a newly introduced lease on life, continue reading to learn how undercut hairstyles can be your ally in style and scalp health.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that is it time to give your hairstyle and scalp a breath of fresh air? Say hello to the undercut hairstyle, a fashion-forward solution that can elevate your look and promote skin health.

It has been revealed that by significantly reducing hair volume, undercuts allow for improved air circulation around the scalp. The result? Less trapped heat and moisture — factors that can contribute to fungal infections, scalp acne, dandruff, and dermatitis.

Whether you’re battling irritation or want to give your “do” a newly introduced lease on life, continue reading to learn how undercut hairstyles can be your ally in style and scalp health.

An undercut involves shaving or cutting hair very short on the sides or back of the head while leaving the hair on top longer.

Originally popular in men’s hairstyling, the undercut has crossed gender boundaries and gained popularity among peeps seeking a hairstyle that stands out.

Sources indicate that it’s a style that offers a stark contrast and is often used to add an edge to an otherwise conventional look. So whether it’s a side undercut, undercut pixie, mullet undercut, or nape undercut, these hairstyles for women, men, and folks of all genders enhance individuality while offering practical benefits like reduced drying time and less hair maintenance.

Choosing an undercut means embracing a hairstyle with a “heady” mix of aesthetic and practical benefits. Here’s why an undercut might be the refreshing change you need.

Ready to turn heads? The standout feature of an undercut is undoubtedly its unique appearance. Hidden under the longer layers, it packs a punch of boldness you can flaunt or conceal — whatever fits your vibe. You can control the reveal, whether you’re showcasing that edgy undercut for a night out or keeping it classy for the office.

Recent findings suggest that got a mane that’s more lioness than laid-back? An undercut might be your upcoming BFF. Strategically shaving or trimming the hair short on the sides or back dramatically dials down the volume. This means your thick, voluminous hair becomes way easier to manage and style, turning a heavy head of hair into something light and breezy.

Sources indicate that and the best part? You get to keep all the styling potential without any of the hassle. It’s a practical solution that doesn’t sacrifice style for comfort.

It has been revealed that are you chasing the clock every morning? An undercut could slash your prep time. With less hair to fuss over, you can breeze through your washing, drying, and styling routine faster than you can say “snooze button.”.

This trimmed-down approach is a time-saver and reduces the daily wear and tear from blow dryers and straighteners, keeping hair healthier in the long run.

Undercuts reduce your scalp’s weight and improve hair follicle airflow. This keeps the scalp cooler and reduces the buildup of sweat and oil that can lead to scalp irritation, dermatitis, and dandruff. As a result, undercuts could lead to more robust, healthier hair growth.

In a recent development, ready to shake up your style with a cool undercut? Here’s a rundown of some options to add a dash of daring to your daily look:.

Are you looking for a dramatic change without total commitment? Try the side-swept undercut.

This style features a sleek shave on one side of the head, just above the ear, while keeping the hair on top and the other side longer.

It’s perfect for folks who love to play with contrast — sweep the top hair over to the shaved side for an instant bold statement.

Sources indicate that if subtlety is more your speed, this undercut is a wicked choice. It’s a shaved area tucked away at the back of the head or underneath the top layer of hair so that it can play a fantastic game of hide-and-seek.

Wear your hair down for a business-as-usual look, or tie it up to reveal a sneaky, stylish surprise. It’s an excellent choice for peeps wanting a touch of edge.

Industry observers note that are you feeling bold and artistic? Design Undercuts take personal expression to the next level. These chic undercuts are masterpieces, boasting intricate geometric patterns, sweet floral motifs, or any design that speaks to you.

Do you prefer a more understated yet stylish look? The tapered undercut starts very short near the ear and gracefully lengthens as it ascends the head, blending with your other locks.

It’s a softer version of the undercut that pairs beautifully with bob or lob cuts and offers a gentle nod to the undercut trend without going full-throttle.

The undercut hair offers both style and substance. It reduces styling time and promotes scalp health. By alleviating the weight and allowing the scalp to breathe, undercuts can help minimize problems like overheating and irritation, especially during warmer months.

Whether you’re drawn to the edgy designs or the subtle tapered style, an undercut could be a clever hack to simplify your morning routine. More time for coffee, less time with the comb!

Hickey Stages: Understanding and Managing Love Bites Effectively

📅 05 Jul 2024 | ⏱️ 4 min read (788 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Greatist

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, hickeys, or as scientists call them, subdermal hematomas, are love’s graffiti.
  • A hickey, medically known as a subdermal contusion or hematoma, is simply a bruise that forms as a result of vigorous kissing or sucking on soft skin, typically around the neck.
  • It has been revealed that from a medical standpoint, hickeys are intriguing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, hickeys, or as scientists call them, subdermal hematomas, are love’s graffiti. If you’ve ever scrambled for scarves or turtlenecks, welcome to the kissing booth of knowledge! Join us as we navigate the lifecycle of hickeys, from their eye-catching start to their subtle fade, and learn how to speed up their departure.

A hickey, medically known as a subdermal contusion or hematoma, is simply a bruise that forms as a result of vigorous kissing or sucking on soft skin, typically around the neck. This intense suction causes the tiny blood vessels under the skin, a.k.a. capillaries, to burst and release blood into the surrounding tissues. The immediate result? An unmistakable red or purple mark that gradually shifts to a darker shade as it heals.

It has been revealed that from a medical standpoint, hickeys are intriguing. They showcase the skin’s sensitivity and the body’s rapid response to minor vascular injury. Not so romantic when you think about it scientifically, right? But hey, it’s all part of the human experience of showing affection — or something like that.

Industry observers note that when you get a hickey, your body starts a healing process that resembles how it deals with other bruises. Here’s a more detailed look at each stage of a hickey’s life cycle.

Immediately after the passionate moment, a hickey appears on the skin, screaming in shades of bright red or deep purple. This initial coloration is due to blood from the ruptured capillaries pooling beneath the skin’s surface in response to the suction. It’s your skin’s way of signaling that there’s been some minor internal damage in that area.

As the hickey begins to heal, it undergoes a whole wardrobe of color transformations, showcasing your body’s metabolic process at work.

Initially, the hickey darkens as the blood begins to oxidize. Then, after a few days, the body starts to break down and reabsorb the blood, so it turns lighter — going from blue to green to brown and, finally, mellow yellow. This rainbow journey reflects the breakdown of hemoglobin, the iron-containing substance in the blood, into biliverdin and bilirubin.

Industry observers note that finally, your hickey starts to ghost you. Over a week or two, depending on factors like your skin type, overall health, how severe the hickey was., and how your body rides the healing waves, the last traces of your hickey fade into nothing.

Recent findings suggest that during this stage, the body’s immune system clears away the remaining by-products of the broken-down blood. White blood cells swoop in like a cleanup crew at a festival, gobbling up and digesting the debris in a process called phagocytosis, while increased blood flow to the area helps to flush out the remnants.

Sources indicate that need a hickey gone yesterday? Here’s how to help your hickey heal. Start with a cold pack — grab a spoon from the freezer or a chilled gel pack and gently press it against your hickey. This will help reduce any swelling and scatter the blood pooling under your skin, which can help minimize that bold bruise.

Sources indicate that after using cold treatment for the first 48 hours, it’s time to turn up the heat. Switch to warm compresses to get the blood flowing smoothly again. A few minutes a few times a day invites more circulation to the hickey zone, helping you hustle through healing and clear out the blood remnants more swiftly.

In a recent development, you can also try a dab of comfrey ointment. Research shows it may reduce bruise size and coloration for some peeps.

Caught off guard? A little concealer or foundation over the hickey makes it less noticeable.

Not into makeup? Scarves and high-necked shirts are also great accessories for your camouflage arsenal.

Typically, a hickey will last anywhere from 5 days to 2 weeks, depending on its severity and your body’s healing capabilities.

In a recent development, communication is key! Let your partner know your feelings about receiving a hickey — some might find it fun, while others may prefer to keep their necks clear.

While generally harmless, hickeys can sometimes lead to complications like skin infections or, very rarely, blood clots. It’s best to keep the affection gentle to avoid any concerns.

Hickeys are nothing more than bruises in disguise. They start as bright red to purple love stamps and gradually fade over several days to a couple of weeks. Speed up the process with heat and cold packs or a splodge of comfrey cream.

Remember, the best approach to handling hickeys — like all aspects of relationships — is communication and care. So go forth, love responsibly, and keep a scarf handy, just in case!

Latest Update: Dezeen Awards 2026 architecture project of the year revealed

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A tree-top sauna that punctures its architectural framework with the surrounding woodland has been named Dezeen Awards 2026 architecture project of the year following the announcement of all 19 architecture category winners at a party in London.
  • The 19 winners awarded at the ninth annual Dezeen Awards ceremony are located in 11 different countries, including Canada, France, India, Japan and Mexico.
  • Daichi Silent River Tree Sauna won the project of the year award in the architecture sector, it was also named leisure and wellness project of the year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A tree-top sauna that punctures its architectural framework with the surrounding woodland has been named Dezeen Awards 2026 architecture project of the year following the announcement of all 19 architecture category winners at a party in London.

The 19 winners awarded at the ninth annual Dezeen Awards ceremony are located in 11 different countries, including Canada, France, India, Japan and Mexico.

Daichi Silent River Tree Sauna won the project of the year award in the architecture sector, it was also named leisure and wellness project of the year.

Leisure and wellness projects win big again.

The judges hailed the biophilic project as “beautifully minimalist with a spiritual touch of the soul”.

“It’s totally fresh, totally innovative, and never seen before,” they added.

The win marks the second consecutive year that the leisure and wellness project of the year has gone on to claim the overall sector title, following Herzog & de Meuron’s win last year.

Silent River Tree Sauna by Daichi.

The winning project of the year was up against category winners including a sprawling brick-clad university building modelled on stepped wells in India, a country house with walls formed of unstabilised rammed earth in the UK and a project featuring an 18-kilometre-long limestone wall that allows wildlife to pass through in Mexico.

A housing project that appears as if emerging from the natural landscape and a viewpoint designed to evoke a giant silver ring left on the burial site of a legendary Viking were also amongst the category winners.

Read more about all the winning architecture projects below:.

Architecture project of the year and leisure and wellness project of the year: Daichi Silent River Tree Sauna by Daichi.

The project is nestled within a forest in Kanagawa, southwest of Tokyo, and forms part of the Daichi Silent River retreat alongside guest cabins and additional sauna spaces.

Leisure and wellness is also about mental health, which this project addresses perfectly.

The idea for the project was to make the trees feel part of the architecture, using them as both supports and the defining feature of the pared-back structure.

“Leisure and wellness is also about mental health, which this project addresses perfectly,” mentioned the master jury.

“It is a building that offers a spiritual connection between humans and nature.”.

House (urban) project of the year: Amami House by Sakai Architects.

Local studio Sakai Architects won urban house of the year for its off-grid home on Amami Ōshima, an island in the Amami archipelago off Japan‘s southern coast.

This house shows how we can live sustainably on a small footprint, in close relationship to nature.

The design was informed by the region’s traditional materials and crafts and its development was spurred by the increase in extreme weather conditions on the island.

“This house shows how we can live sustainably on a small footprint, in close relationship to nature,” the master jury noted.

“In a time of climate crisis, it offers an excellent solution for autonomy of energy, while smartly reinterpreting the arrangement and materials of a traditional Japanese house.”.

House (rural) project of the year: Jiang Deng Lu by Shisuo Design Office.

Shisuo Design Office won rural house of the year for Jiang Deng Lu in Anhui, China.

This project sits very delicately in its context and is beautiful as a result.

The compact building is raised partially on stilts to look as though it is floating above its sloped riverside site and made using stainless-steel offcuts salvaged from the client’s own factory.

“This project sits very delicately in its context and is beautiful as a result,” stated the judges.

“Innovative in its use of available materials, the project is highly resolved, with incredible quality of light and generosity of space despite a small footprint.”.

Housing project of the year: La Querola by Ribas & Ribas Arquitectos.

Ribas & Ribas Arquitectos won housing project of the year for La Querola in Ordino, Andorra.

A deliberate provocation against the salami-type housing where repetition is at the core.

Made up of seven irregularly shaped blocks embedded into the sloping valley and clad in locally sourced slate, the building’s facades feature recessed windows and openings revealing outdoor terraces.

The judges commended the development’s trend-bucking design as a “deliberately expressionist project, celebrating forms that are not repeatable”.

“It’s a deliberate provocation against the salami-type housing where repetition is at the core. It’s unconventional, unique, controversial, and a very strong statement,” they noted.

Recently, a fire damaged all seven buildings in the uninhabited development. The project also won its category for the 2026 public vote.

House renovation of the year: Haniyasu House by Aatismo.

Local architecture studio Aatismo won house renovation of the year for Haniyasu House, a home in the coastal town of Kamakura, Japan.

It is aesthetic but also functional, cleverly improving seismic stability.

The project saw the single-storey home, originally built in 1967, stripped back to its timber frame after a typhoon had left it structurally unsound, and boldly characterised with rough walls streaked with clay, soil and metal powders to evoke ceramic glazes.

The judges praised the project’s sensitivity to “the history of both the architecture and its owners”.

“It is aesthetic but also functional, cleverly improving seismic stability,” they added.

House extension of the year: Golmorad by ZAV Architects.

Iranian studio ZAV Architects won house extension of the year for its project featuring a series of overlapping arches shifts in colour from terracotta to blue in Tehran, Iran.

It’s clever and fun, with colours that reveal an intent to enjoy life.

Transforming the residence from a weekend villa into a permanent home, its arched series of overlapping arched roofs appears as if organically growing from the home.

The judges found the extension to be “playful with a sense of freedom,” adding that, “it doesn’t manipulate the old house in any way, but instead seems to organically extend it in a very unpredictable direction.”.

“It’s clever and fun, with colours that reveal an intent to enjoy life,” they stated.

The project also won its category for the 2026 public vote.

Civic project of the year: Zando Central Market by Think Tank Architecture.

French studio Think Tank Architecture won civic project of the year for its geometric brick-and-concrete market in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo.

A bold and strong project with really interesting architectural moves.

The latest building, with space for 20,000 vendors, replaces a historic market on the same site in the capital that was demolished after insufficient maintenance and an overwhelming number of vendors left it unfit for purpose.

“A bold and strong project with really interesting architectural moves, and a capacity to serve the community in a really large-scale way,” stated the master jury.

“It has a variety within it to allow a lot of activity to take place, with materials that are simple but sustainable.”.

Cultural project of the year: Ismaili Center Houston by Farshid Moussavi Architecture.

Farshid Moussavi Architects won cultural project of the year for its Ismaili Center in Houston, United States.

A very successful community space that has reinterpreted and reimagined the Ismaili-centric typology in a very contemporary rather than self-referential manner.

The building and its sprawling gardens is the first Ismaili Center in the US and is one of several around the world commissioned by the current Imam, or spiritual leader, of the Shia Ismaili Muslim community to serve as a place of worship and cultural exchange.

The judges praised it as a “very successful community space that has reinterpreted and reimagined the Ismaili-centric typology in a very contemporary rather than self-referential manner”.

“It has a stunning relationship to light, and incredible detailing and materiality,” they added.

Workplace project (small) of the year: Carpenter’s Home by Primary Architects.

Chinese studio Primary Architects won small workplace project of the year for its undulating timber roof-topped studio in Xinyang, China.

The architecture speaks of its function, offering space that cleverly facilitates different activities.

The project, a local carpenter’s studio, was designed by the practice to incorporate the craftsman’s studio, as well as a woodcraft workshop that is also open to the public.

“A beautiful project that goes above and beyond the brief,” commended the judges.

“The architecture speaks of its function, offering space that cleverly facilitates different activities.”.

Workplace project (large) of the year: Florentia Village by Turner Works.

Architecture studio Turner Works won large workplace project of the year for Florentia Village, London.

Well-thought out in terms of programme, layout and use of materials and colour.

The practice transformed an old textile manufacturing site in London’s Harringay Warehouse District into a creative hub that offers flexible workshops, studios and industrial units ranging from 46 to 1,400 square metres, alongside community spaces and a cafe.

The judges praised it as “well-thought out in terms of programme, layout and use of materials and colour,” as well as the buildings being “highly flexible, with spaces designed to reinforce a sense of community”.

The project also won its category for the 2026 public vote.

Education project of the year: Prestige University by Sanjay Puri Architects.

Sanjay Puri Architects won education project of the year for its sprawling brick-clad university building in Indore, India.

In a country with a tradition of beautiful campuses, but where most latest constructions are based on western typologies, this one breaks the mould.

Referencing traditional stepped wells found in the country, its defining feature is its 9,000-square-metre walkable roof, which comprises 463 stepped platforms that can be used as individual social spaces or as a singular auditorium for up to 9,000 people.

“This project creates its own universe,” said the master jury.

“In a country with a tradition of beautiful campuses, but where most newly introduced constructions are based on western typologies, this one breaks the mould,” they continued.

“The massing of the roof reduces scale and creates interesting courtyards, creating spaces that feel appropriate for both the place and its climate.”.

The project also won its category for the 2026 public vote.

Heritage project of the year: Olympics Utilities by Chartier-Corbasson Architects.

French studio Chartier-Corbasson Architectes won heritage project of the year for its transformation of a neglected underground passage beneath Paris, France.

It was a joy to see so much love put into a building typology that we might typically consider unimportant.

Located in a passage beneath the Trocadero Gardens, the studio created a public restroom, using an industrial-feeling palette of stainless and weathered steel to highlight its thoughtful, utilitarian design while giving it a latest purpose.

“It was a joy to see so much love put into a building typology that we might typically consider unimportant,” remarked the judges.

Recent findings suggest that “The project creates architectural character, while also preserving a connection to 19th-century futuristic architecture. Unusual, but iconic.”.

Hospitality project of the year: Perma by Mold Architects.

Perma by Mold Architects in Serifos, Greece won hospitality project of the year, sponsored by Sanderson.

There is an economy of means in its relationship to the topography, which cleverly reduces the overall footprint.

Comprising five guest houses, the rugged retreat on the island of Serifos was constructed by using material extracted during construction to build much of the retreat itself, rather than removing the hillside and building on top of it.

The judges praised its “striking architecture”, noting it as “very innovative in its programmatic possibilities”.

“There is an economy of means in its relationship to the topography, which cleverly reduces the overall footprint,” they stated.

The project also won its category for the 2026 public vote.

Infrastructure and transport project of the year: Naples Underground Central Station by Miralles Tagliabue EMBT.

Spanish architecture studio EMBT won infrastructure and transport project of the year for Naples Underground Central Station in Italy.

A rich environment to spend time in, not just catch a train.

Contrasting its modernist surroundings with a wavy timber roof, the 10,000-square-metre building was designed to replace a previously understated metro entrance with a upcoming public plaza that felt more integrated with the surrounding city.

The judges commended the project as a “successful urban space, both elegant and spatially interesting.”.

In a recent development, “A rich environment to spend time in, not just catch a train,” they continued. “The use of timber is also impressive.”.

Small project of the year: Ring of Bjólfur by Arkibygg Architects.

Local studios Arkibygg Architects and Esja Architecture won small project of the year for their mountain viewpoint in Seyðisfjörður, Iceland.

A minimal intervention that choreographs the discovery of a landscape in a simple but sophisticated way.

Designed to evoke a giant silver ring left on the alleged burial site of a legendary Viking, the viewpoint improves access to a ridge on Mount Bjólfur and celebrates its varied views over the town, valley and surrounding peaks.

The master jury hailed the viewpoint as a “minimal intervention that choreographs the discovery of a landscape in a simple but sophisticated way,” adding that, “the minimal use of material maximises the experience”.

Mixed-use project of the year: York Minster Centre of Excellence by Tonkin Liu.

Architecture studio Tonkin Liu won mixed-use project of the year for its two timber buildings on either side of a Grade I-listed Gothic cathedral in York, United Kingdom.

The materiality speaks to the programming of the building, inspiring a new generation of makers using the space.

Named The Centre of Excellence for Heritage Craft Skills, the buildings include the rectangular Heritage Quad and the triangular Technology Hub, both of which give working stonemasons views of the historic York Minster cathedral.

“There is a real honesty in the combination of buildings, with a unique roofing structure,” mentioned the judges.

“The materiality speaks to the programming of the building, inspiring a upcoming generation of makers using the space,” they added.

Landscape and urban design of the year: Parque del Jaguar by Colectivo C733.

Mexican studio Colectivo C733 won landscape and urban design of the year for its work across Parque del Jaguar in Tulum, Mexico.

Despite limited budget and materials, the interventions create an intimate experience with the landscape, successfully addressing water scarcity, indigenous planting and flexibility for different community projects.

The project aims to safeguard one of the region’s important habitats for jaguars, whose movement through the landscape had become disrupted by roads, development and tourism.

It features an 18-kilometre-long limestone wall that allows wildlife to pass through while protecting more than 1,000 hectares of forest, as well as a network of boundaries, access points and visitor facilities intended to protect the animals’ habitat while allowing people to explore the area.

The judges praised the project as “rooted in its context, made for locals as well as tourists,” adding that, “despite limited budget and materials, the interventions create an intimate experience with the landscape, successfully addressing water scarcity, indigenous planting and flexibility for different community projects.”.

Sustainable building of the year: Rammed Earth House by Tuckey Design Studio.

Rammed Earth house by Tuckey Design Studio in Wiltshire, United Kingdom, won sustainable building of the year, sponsored by Michelmersh.

Although large for a two-person house, it is an incredible testbed that could pave the way for more rammed earth architecture in Europe.

Built on the site of a former brickworks, the rural country house was constructed from both the clay underfoot and an aggregate made from crushed demolition waste to form unstabilised rammed earth walls.

As a form of earth construction that is largely untested at such scale in the UK, the judges commended the project as “a radical example of material innovation”.

“Although large for a two-person house, it is an incredible testbed that could pave the way for more rammed earth architecture in Europe,” they mentioned.

The project also won its category for the 2026 public vote.

Sustainable renovation of the year: De Nederlandsche Bank by Mecanoo.

Dutch firm Mecanoo won sustainable renovation of the year for its major renovation of the Netherlands’ central bank in Amsterdam.

An admirable transformation of a brutalist-era building.

The project involved dismantling a 14-storey tower and opening up the former gold vault, seeing a complete retrofit of De Nederlandsche Bank, a 1968 structure that some had described as the nation’s ugliest building.

The renovation was praised as “an admirable transformation of a brutalist-era building,” by the master jury, who also noted its efforts to adapt it to a different use “while also addressing material and energy concerns.”.

Latest Update: Bye-Bye Bites: 14 Ways to Get Rid of Mosquito Bites Overnight

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, wondering how to get rid of mosquito bites overnight?
  • According to recent reports, if you’re caught without bug bite cream or ointment, don’t worry — plenty of simple home remedies can provide quick relief.
  • Just as you’d ice an injury, icing a bug bite can help decrease inflammation and temporarily numb the pain.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, wondering how to get rid of mosquito bites overnight? Discover simple home remedies for quick relief. From crushed ice to aloe vera, explore easy solutions to soothe itching and inflammation for a peaceful night’s sleep.

According to recent reports, if you’re caught without bug bite cream or ointment, don’t worry — plenty of simple home remedies can provide quick relief. From soothing aloe vera to the calming effects of oatmeal, discover easy solutions to alleviate itching and inflammation so you can sleep peacefully.

Just as you’d ice an injury, icing a bug bite can help decrease inflammation and temporarily numb the pain.

If icy cold treatments aren’t your vibe, you can apply heat instead to soothe your bump.

Industry observers note that aloe vera gel does more than soothe sunburns! It can also help ease bug bites and help them heal.

According to recent reports, baking soda can remove the itch. To make a paste, mix 1 tablespoon of it with a splash of water (not too much). Apply it to your bite as you would zit cream. Keep it on for 10 minutes before rinsing it off.

Did you know basil (yes, like the kind in your pasta) has a rich history as a skin infection remedy? It contains antioxidants that may bring down bug bite inflammation.

To whip up your own basil rub, boil a couple cups of water with 1/2 ounce of dried basil leaves. Cool the mixture before applying it to a washcloth and gently massaging it onto the bite for sweet relief.

You already know apple cider vinegar (fermented liquid from apples) is a huge player in the natural remedy world.

Some people use it to clean due to its antimicrobial effects, and others mix it into food or drinks for its possible health benefits (like helping with blood sugar issues).

Its beauty with bites is that it can help ease burning or stinging while disinfecting your scratchy little bump.

Onion juice (while not delicious) has antifungal and antibacterial properties, which could possibly help ward off infection. Plus, it could make your bite sting less. Just dab a bit of raw onion juice onto your bites. The downside? We’re not sure how well it works … and it’s kinda stinky.

Thyme has been used to help with skin concerns for a long time. You can use it to help decrease irritation by chopping it up and applying the teeny leaves directly to your bite for 10 minutes. You can also boil thyme, soak a cloth in the cooled liquid, and wrap it around your bite.

Peppermint oil may work as an anti-itch agent. Mix it with carrier oil (like olive oil) before applying it to your skin, though!

Sources indicate that another natural anti-itcher and astringent, lemon balm, may be helpful. You can either apply a lemon balm cream or chop up the leaves and apply them right to the bite.

Witch hazel is a natural wonder with many uses for skin concerns such as acne and psoriasis. It can tackle inflammation and burning while helping your bug bite heal.

This herb may work, but the science is a little dicey. On its own, arnica is toxic, so any over-the-counter products you find have been carefully diluted for your safety.

Sources indicate that the yummy tea that calms and soothes at bedtime has many other uses, including potentially calming an irritated bug bite. Steep the tea bag for 20 minutes before squeezing it out and applying it to your bite once it’s cooled.

Recent findings suggest that blend minced garlic with petroleum jelly or fragrance-free lotion. Place the mixture on your bite for 10 minutes before removing it and applying a cool cloth.

Icing the bite for 10 minutes and then placing a mixture of baking soda and water on it for 10 minutes is a strong choice.

Though not tested for this purpose, some people turn to Vicks to soothe mosquito bites. It’s possible that its antibacterial and anti-inflammatory properties could help heal and soothe mosquito bites. But FYI, this product isn’t considered the best defense against mosquito bites.

Some toothpastes are cooling, so that sensation may offer temporary relief. Some people use toothpaste on insect bites since many toothpastes contain astringents, which can help shrink tissues.

In a recent development, using repellent to prevent bug bites is a good idea. PSA: DEET and lemon eucalyptus oil are safe ways to repel insects.

According to recent reports, mosquitoes are low-key little monsters that cause the most insect bites worldwide. Most bites aren’t serious, but mosquitoes can potentially carry diseases.

Recent findings suggest that ointments, creams, or simple home remedies can help stop the pesky itch after bites. But remember that some natural substances can cause allergic reactions. That said, it’s always a good idea to do a patch test first.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dezeen has confirmed the six winners of Dezeen Awards 2026 Designers of the Year at this evening’s ceremony in London, which include Lina Ghotmeh, Keiji Ashizawa and Yinka Ilori.

Our Designers of the Year awards recognise the best emerging and established talent whose innovative work has made a notable impact on the industry across architecture, interiors and design.

This year, Ghotmeh took home the architect of the year award, while studio duo Shohei Kuma and Elsa Escobedo were named emerging architect of the year.

Interior designer of the year was awarded to Tokyo-based Ashizawa, and Australian designer Yasmine Ghoniem was named emerging interior designer of the year.

London-based Ilori won designer of the year with Stockholm-based Simon Skinner named emerging designer of the year.

Read more about the Designers of the Year below:.

Her poetic approach to materials, memory and landscape brings buildings to life with a rare sensitivity to people, place and planet.

Architect of the year: Lina Ghotmeh.

Industry observers note that ghotmeh, who is the founder of architecture practice Lina Ghotmeh Architecture, is one of the world’s most sought-after architects. Among her high-profile projects was the 2023 Serpentine Pavilion and she was recently appointed to renovate the British Museum’s Western Range galleries.

“From Beirut to Paris and beyond, Lina Ghotmeh creates architecture that feels both rooted in history and entirely of the future,” mentioned the judges.

“Her poetic approach to materials, memory and landscape brings buildings to life with a rare sensitivity to people, place and planet. We anticipate her studio continuing to go from strength to strength.”.

In a recent development, ghotmeh is known for her sustainable and historically rooted designs, including the Stone Garden apartment block in Beruit, which was named architecture project of the year at Dezeen Awards 2021. She has received multiple accolades, including being named on the Time100 Next list in 2025 and winning the 2023 Great Arab Minds Award.

Working between Japan and Europe, Kuma and Elsa are creating an architectural vocabulary that feels both regionally distinctive and deeply connected to its surroundings.

Emerging architect of the year: Shohei Kuma and Elsa Escobedo.

Founded by Japanese architect Shohei Kuma and French‑Spanish architect and urban designer Elsa Escobedo, Kuma&Elsa is an emerging architecture studio with offices in France, Spain and Japan.

“Shohei Kuma and Elsa Escobedo’s emerging practice brings a fresh sense of curiosity to architecture, balancing bold forms and material experimentation with tactility and unexpected gestures,” said the judges.

“Working between Japan and Europe, Kuma and Elsa are creating an architectural vocabulary that feels both regionally distinctive and deeply connected to its surroundings.”.

Among the studio’s varied and intriguing work is Nakano House in Japan’s Fukuoka prefecture – an apartment block informed by the design of a traditional Japanese engawa.

His distinct spaces reveal the beauty in restraint, proving that the most powerful interiors are often those that will quietly stand the test of time.

Interior designer of the year: Keiji Ashizawa.

Interior designer Ashizawa runs his interdisciplinary, craft-oriented studio based on the ideal of “honest design”. Along with interior spaces, his Tokyo-based studio designs everything from lighting to furniture and products.

“Prolific designer Keiji Ashizawa brings a quiet confidence to interior design, where natural materials, considered details, refined craftsmanship and a sense of calm take centre stage,” remarked the judges.

“His distinct spaces reveal the beauty in restraint, proving that the most powerful interiors are often those that will quietly stand the test of time.”.

Recent work from the studio includes a tea shop in central Shanghai, a holiday home clad in charred cedar in central Japan and a showroom for Japanese furniture brand Karimoku.

Often challenging convention, her interiors are expressive and distinctive, and full of character, warmth and individuality that defy easy categorisation.

Emerging interior designer of the year: Yasmine Ghoniem.

Australian designer Ghoniem has found great success since founding her interior studio YSG in 2020 with the aim of creating bold, holistic design experiences.

“Yasmine Ghoniem takes a bold, instinctive approach to interior design, bringing together rich textures, unexpected colour and cultural references,” stated the judges.

“Often challenging convention, her interiors are expressive and distinctive, and full of character, warmth and individuality that defy easy categorisation.”.

Among her recent – and varied – designs are a wellness hotel in Bali, the revamp of a Sydney apartment, a warehouse conversion in Sydney designed to evoke the Mojave desert and a bar for gin brand Four Pillars.

Rooted in his British-Nigerian heritage, his exuberant work reminds us that design can be as joyful as it is meaningful, bringing people together through shared experiences and bold creative expression.

Designer of the year: Yinka Ilori.

Ilori designs pavilions, installations, pop-ups, products and furniture, all united by a bold use of colour informed by his Nigerian heritage.

“Yinka Ilori injects design with an irresistible dose of colour, humour and optimism, turning everyday objects and spaces into lively celebrations of culture and community,” noted the judges.

“Rooted in his British-Nigerian heritage, his exuberant work reminds us that design can be as joyful as it is meaningful, bringing people together through shared experiences and bold creative expression.”.

According to recent reports, ilori has designed numerous pavilions, including the Colour Palace in London and an events space for the Estrel Berlin hotel in Germany. On a smaller scale, he has designed products including a watch for Swiss brand MB&F and his own range of branded homeware.

He also recently created an extensive collection of furniture, fabrics and homeware for Dunelm.

Simon Skinner is a burgeoning talent who brings a fresh perspective to contemporary Scandinavian design, pairing a thoughtful approach to materials with a refined, understated visual language.

Emerging designer of the year: Simon Skinner.

Swedish designer Skinner is well-known for his furniture, sculpture and installations that explore how materials can be rethought or reused.

Recent findings suggest that “Simon Skinner is a burgeoning talent who brings a fresh perspective to contemporary Scandinavian design, pairing a thoughtful approach to materials with a refined, understated visual language. His work subverts the familiar, creating distinct upcoming objects that hint at an exciting new direction for design.”.

Recent examples of his varied, multidisciplinary work include a range of sculptural lights made from second-hand bowls, ashtrays and cat figurines.

Dezeen Awards 2026 in partnership with TrimbleDezeen Awards is the ultimate accolade for architects and designers worldwide. The ninth edition of the annual awards is in partnership with global technology firm Trimble. Through connected hardware and software solutions, Trimble helps designers to transform the way they shape spaces and buildings as well as drive productivity in the process. Trimble’s collaboration with Dezeen Awards demonstrates its ongoing commitment to inspiring and supporting creative excellence across the globe.

Design software Canva's latest advance is an 'AI off' switch

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (710 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Creativebloq

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Over the past couple of years, most of the press releases coming from software companies have contained announcements of newly introduced AI features.
  • Industry observers note that canva is one of those companies, and it's introduced a bunch of generative AI tools to its design platform.
  • Sources indicate that canva has added two AI controls for both Free and Pro people.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Over the past couple of years, most of the press releases coming from software companies have contained announcements of newly introduced AI features. Image, video and vector generation, removal tools, agentic workflows, AI assistants, and myriad other advances that can help artists do in seconds something that used to take hours.

Industry observers note that canva is one of those companies, and it's introduced a bunch of generative AI tools to its design platform. So the email I received yesterday made me do a double take. On the day that Anthropic completed the world's biggest IPO in history, it introduced an 'AI off switch'.

Sources indicate that canva has added two AI controls for both Free and Pro people. The generative AI switch can be used to hide all of its generative AI tools, including Magic Write, Magic Design, Magic Expand, Dream Lab and Canva Code. It can be switched on or off at any time.

Recent findings suggest that there's also an option to “See less AI content” on Canva's library of templates and design elements. This addresses complaints about the glut of AI-generated content making it harder to find quality work, something that's been causing problems on platforms as varied as Etsy and ArtStation.

It has been revealed that canva says AI-generated content remains a "small portion" of its library and that such content is identified in its metadata. Turning on the latest function isn't guaranteed to remove it completely, but it should put human-made templates and design elements first in search results and recommendations.

According to recent reports, the addition of a couple of toggles to the UI wouldn't normally be breaking news, so the fact that Canva feels this deserved its own announcement is telling. After heavily promoting AI tools, it's now presenting the ability to turn them off as a groundbreaking advance – and it is. This might be the first time that a major AI-forward creative software developer has recognised that a sizable portion of its user base just isn't into it.

Recent findings suggest that an 'AI off button' is something that some creatives have been calling for. Part of the difficulty in implementing one is that it needs a definition of AI. Programs like Adobe's Photoshop have used machine learning for many years; it just wasn't branded as 'AI'. Many artists welcome tools that speed up their work, but not ones that do the creation part for them, especially if they're powered by models that were trained on unlicensed work.

According to recent reports, canva's recognised that. The toggle only turns off generative AI tools, such as ones that generate new imagery, text or code from prompts. Assistive editing tools like Background Remover or Magic Grab, which lets you select and move an object in an image will still be available. Using them won't cause your work to be shamed with metadata identifying it as AI-generated.

In a recent development, A 'no AI button' also requires a willingness from the provider. Since generative AI features are often charged on a per-use basis via credits, software companies generally want to encourage their customers to use them.

Adobe teased some impressive-looking AI-powered tools in the Adobe Max Sneaks presentation last week, but it's also clear that some customers detest generative AI, which has created a market for fresh tools like the artist-led Niva app, which is promoting itself as AI-free art software.

Will an AI-off button let Canva have its cake and eat it?

You can learn more about Canva on the website.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Spanish design practice Isern Serra combined organic architectural forms with a vibrant colour palette for Circl, a fitness studio and matcha cafe located in Barcelona’s historic Eixample district.
  • Set just below street level, the 180-square-metre space was designed to offer an escape from the busy city centre and contains an entrance cafe, reception area, changing rooms, bathrooms and a pilates studio.
  • “The project began with the idea of bringing together two worlds: pilates and matcha,” Isern Serra told Dezeen.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Photography by Salva López.

Spanish design practice Isern Serra combined organic architectural forms with a vibrant colour palette for Circl, a fitness studio and matcha cafe located in Barcelona’s historic Eixample district.

Set just below street level, the 180-square-metre space was designed to offer an escape from the busy city centre and contains an entrance cafe, reception area, changing rooms, bathrooms and a pilates studio.

“The project began with the idea of bringing together two worlds: pilates and matcha,” Isern Serra told Dezeen.

“Although different in nature, both share a common philosophy centred on wellbeing, balance and the connection between body and mind,” he continued.

“Architecture plays an essential role in this experience, accompanying visitors on a gradual transition from the energy of the city towards a more intimate and introspective environment.”.

His studio introduced a series of colour-blocked spaces to guide customers through different phases of the interior, with colours that were specifically chosen to correspond to the function and tone of each area.

“This vision of wellbeing takes shape through a carefully choreographed sequence of spaces, where each change in level, colour and atmosphere guides customers away from the bustle of the city and towards an increasingly introspective environment,” stated Serra.

Sources indicate that serra combined cream banquette seating with dark wooden tables and alabaster sconces to create a calm, meditative environment for the cafe part of the space. A sculptural, mirrored service counter was also incorporated to reflect natural light around the space.

To signal the transition into the pilates studio, the designers introduced a deep-green reception hallway with tiered seating blocks and a spherical light installation.

The bright green circulation area is connected by an open archway and features curved architectural volumes that house the changing rooms, bathrooms and a water fountain.

Another rounded archway then leads to the main studio.

The main pilates studio was designed as a white space to reflect the coloured light from a sculptural LED light installation attached to the vaulted ceiling.

The aim was to create diverse exercise environments and enable the lighting to control the mood and energy of the space.

“The white surfaces act as a neutral canvas for coloured light, allowing different hues to transform the atmosphere,” Serra noted.

“This system also offers flexibility for brand collaborations, as the lighting can be adapted to reflect different identities and experiences,” he added.

In the studio, the designers used mirrored walls to create the illusion of a circular room and added full-length perimeter curtains to soften the space’s texture.

Other interior projects recently featured on Dezeen include Matteo Thun designs for Milan’s Torre Velasca skyscraper and SABO’s design of an apartment on Manhattan’s Lower East Side.

Photography by Salva López.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

L-tyrosine is an amino acid (AKA protein building block) that supports your body, from your muscles to your noggin.

It’s a non-essential amino acid, which means your body can make it on its own, so you don’t have to get it from food.

That being said, consuming foods high in L-tyrosine or taking supplements could have extra cognitive and physical benefits – here’s what to know.

According to recent reports, L-tyrosine is an amino acid that the body produces naturally. Though your bod can prob create enough of the stuff on its own, some research suggests that supplementing with it can boost your mood and help regulate your stress response.

L-tyrosine helps make many vital chemical messengers, such as:.

Supplementing with L-tyrosine is believed by some to boost levels of dopamine, adrenalin, and norepinephrine in particular.

Foods naturally high in tyrosine include:.

L-tyrosine may improve your memory and mental alertness. Since L-tyrosine increases dopamine availability in your body, experts think it may boost your cognitive performance. In addition to reward centers, dopamine is linked to working memory processes and plays a key role in the brain’s aging process.

In a 2019 review of several studies, researchers found that a higher intake of L-tyrosine was linked to improved cognition. It also improved executive functions like brain flexibility, convergent thinking, and reasoning.

However, researchers noted that L-tyrosine is most effective when dopamine and norepinephrine levels are reduced (which basically means when you feel stressed AF).

Some L-tyrosine supplement companies claim that their products are both mood boosters and antidepressants, but the results are mixed.

L-tyrosine increases dopamine, the feel-good hormone that’s linked to reward processing and also addiction. In general, it’s been shown to be a vital regulator of mood, behavior, and brainpower – so it makes sense that getting enough of it could benefit your mood, too.

However, the research on supplementation of tyrosine for depression is super dated, so it’s challenging to draw any definitive conclusions RN. (Plus, depression is also a super complex condition that involves more than just dopamine depletion.).

And though there are some people dubbing L-tyrosine “natural Adderall” for its purported beneficial effect on ADHD, so far, there’s no research to support these claims yet, either. (Though it *is* true that there seems to be a link between ADHD and altered dopamine levels.).

Phenylketonuria is a rare genetic disorder in which the body can’t properly process another essential amino acid, phenylalanine.

Since those with the disorder may also be deficient in L-tyrosine, some experts think that supplementing with it could help relieve some symptoms like seizures or skin rashes.

However, according to a 2021 review of several studies, there is not enough evidence to say for sure.

The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) considers taking L-tyrosine supplements generally safe.

That being said, it’s not recommended to mix with the following medications:.

It’s not advisable to take it if you’re pregnant or breastfeeding.

In a recent development, research suggests that L-tyrosine supplementation likely benefits your brainpower under stress. It also may benefit conditions like depression, but more research is needed to know for sure.

Like any supplement, it is a good idea to contact your healthcare provider before adding it to your medicine cabinet, especially if you have preexisting health conditions or take medications.

Latest Update: This artist-made Photoshop alternative has no AI and no subscription

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (740 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Creativebloq

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Adobe software might still rule in many industries, but there's a growing number of alternatives, from Canva's free Affinity to open-source Krita, Maxon's Autograph for motion design and DaVinci Resolve for video editing.
  • According to recent reports, NIVA is clean and light, works in your browser and it's led by a conceptual artist rather than a software developer.
  • It has been revealed that like the recent AI-coded Adobe clones, NIVA was born out of a frustration with the direction of a certain Californian software giant.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Adobe software might still rule in many industries, but there's a growing number of alternatives, from Canva's free Affinity to open-source Krita, Maxon's Autograph for motion design and DaVinci Resolve for video editing. Into the fray, comes a fresh artist-led app who's main selling points include the fact that it DOESN'T have any generative AI tools.

According to recent reports, NIVA is clean and light, works in your browser and it's led by a conceptual artist rather than a software developer. After it was announced on Instagram this week, it picked up close to 30,000 customers in 48 hours.

It has been revealed that like the recent AI-coded Adobe clones, NIVA was born out of a frustration with the direction of a certain Californian software giant. But it takes a very different approach. It wasn't vibe coded, and it doesn't attempt to replicate the look, feel or functions of any one existing program.

The project's led by Stuart Semple, an artist who previously annoyed Anish Kapoor by creating a very black shade of black.

"With Adobe pushing AI further into its tools, I wanted somewhere people could still practise their craft and make things themselves. No AI doing it for them," he states. "NIVA is very much our own thing that we've all built together.

Having previously made FREETONE, a free alternative to Pantone colours, with Culture Hustle, he started a Kickstarter for a project that was initially called Abode. He raised $240,000 from 3,000 backers, a few hundred of whom have been using the software regularly over a year and a half of beta testing. Around 10 people were involved more heavily in making the software, but Stuart says he largely built it himself "with help from some geeky friends from time to time when I've got stuck.".

At some point the name changed, and the project became NIVA. "I can't say I woke up to a nasty letter from the lawyers representing Adobe for legal reasons, so I won't," Stuart comments.

It has been revealed that NIVA has many of the core tools and functionalities of a program like Photoshop. There are brushes, a pen tool with boolean ops, cloning and healing tools, layers, curve adjustments and blend modes, type tools with kerning, layouts and gradients.

But it's lighter, with a more minimalist UI and fewer menus despite providing the ability to draw vectors, manipulate photos and lay out text and pages all in a single app. Owners also get a portfolio page, and there's a visual asset library called Storehouse, where you can store, sort, search and share work. Work can be exported in formats including PDF and SVG.

The pricing model is refreshing too. There's no subscription, and NIVA is free to use for an hour a day. You can buy full-day passes for $10 a time, or you can buy permanent access for $100. If you buy a day pass and later go permanent, the price of the day pass will be discounted. This allows a full opportunity to try the software before committing.

The response so far has been more enthusiastic than Stuart ever imagined. "I'm so excited and a bit freaked out", he admits, adding that what he finds most encouraging is that over half of the people who used NIVA in those first 48 hours made something with it within 40 seconds of getting access.

Sources indicate that "We're finally at a stage where it's stable enough and good enough to share with the world," he adds. It's only version one, the start of something I hope will be great. I still have loads I want to do with it".

You can use the software online at NIVA.design.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Photography by Takuya Yamauchi.

Mexican design firms Esrawe Studio and Cadena Concepts divided the interior of this concrete building in Tokyo, designed for perfume brand Xinú, with angular black-timber displays.

Esrawe Studio and Cadena Concepts designed the timber elements as sculptural interventions that also organise the interior of the three-storey shop, which is located in the city’s Aoyama neighbourhood.

The black-laminated wooden planks span the interior walls at jaunty angles, as if puncturing the building, which was originally designed by Japanese studio Satoshi Hirano.

“We approached the project as an intervention within an existing building, rather than simply designing an interior,” stated Esrawe Studio founder Héctor Esrawe, who also co-founded Xinú.

“By introducing a continuous architectural structure that traverses its different levels, appearing and disappearing throughout the volume, we intended to generate a new perception of the original architecture,” he told Dezeen.

“Both structures coexist, establishing a dialogue between what was already there and what has been introduced, creating an unexpected spatial experience.”.

Long, overlapping shelves with mirrored accents display products on the ground floor, which is dedicated to body perfume.

Xinú’s room scents are located on the first floor, where hand-painted brass panels on the walls and ceilings add a touch of warmth to the concrete and black-timber surfaces.

Aiming to reveal the processes behind the perfume products, the top floor displays botanical specimens, raw materials, found objects and collages in drawers.

Esrawe Studio also designed cabinet drawers to reference the storage and organisation typically found in natural history museums, intending to give visitors a feeling of discovery when interacting with the furniture.

“For Xinú, architecture has never been conceived simply as a backdrop for products, but as an essential part of how they are experienced,” said Esrawe.

“Our intention is to create spaces that encourage curiosity, discovery and a more intimate relationship with objects, materials and scent,” he continued.

“In Tokyo, the inserted architectural structures move beyond conventional retail display, becoming sculptural elements that enhance the presence of the objects.”.

Xinú Tokyo is the latest branch Esrawe Studio and Cadena Concepts have designed for the perfume brand. Other shops include a radial wooden pavilion in Mexico City and a showroom in Oaxaca informed by basalt rock formations.

Photography by Takuya Yamauchi.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • For all the hype surrounding GLP-1 weight loss medications like Wegovy and Zepbound, these drugs don’t work for everyone.
  • It’s called retatrutide, and it’s a triple-agonist medication, which means it acts on three different receptors in the body.
  • Recent findings suggest that retatrutide is already being hailed as a game changer in an area of health that’s already welcomed plenty of impressive medications in the past few years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For all the hype surrounding GLP-1 weight loss medications like Wegovy and Zepbound, these drugs don’t work for everyone. Nearly 17% of people on these medications are considered “non-responders,” leaving them looking for a different solution. But there’s a buzzy upcoming medication waiting in the wings. While it’s not yet approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), people are already seeking it out.

It’s called retatrutide, and it’s a triple-agonist medication, which means it acts on three different receptors in the body. By comparison, Wegovy (semaglutide) acts on one receptor, while Zepbound (tirzepatide) works on two.

Recent findings suggest that retatrutide is already being hailed as a game changer in an area of health that’s already welcomed plenty of impressive medications in the past few years. In fact, clinical trial results show that it’s so effective for weight loss that some people have dropped out of the trials because they felt that they lost too much weight.

According to recent reports, but retatrutide is still being tested in clinical trials. Eli Lilly, which makes reatrutide and Zepbound, hasn’t even submitted the trial results yet to the FDA for approval. So this is still an experimental medication—and versions of it are being sold online for cheap.

Mir Ali, MD, medical director of MemorialCare Surgical Weight Loss Center at Orange Coast Medical Center in Fountain Valley, California, tells SELF that retatrutide is “not really available” for use just yet, short of signing up for a clinical trial. There is no set timeline for when it will hit the market, given that clinical trial results have not yet been submitted to the FDA.

Industry observers note that if you’ve struggled with losing weight on a GLP-1 medication or just want to pay significantly less for what appears to be the next big thing in weight loss drugs, it’s understandable to be tempted to add this to your cart. Here’s why doctors recommend resisting the urge.

Retatrutide is similar to GLP-1 medications in a few ways. Namely, it’s used for weight loss and is given once a week through an injection. Like Wegovy, Ozempic, and Zepbound, retatrutide works by reducing appetite and slowing digestion.

But retatrutide has more going on than that. This medication acts on three hormone receptors in the body—glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), gastric inhibitory polypeptide (GIP), and glucagon (GCG). “This is the first one in the pipeline to work on three different receptors,” claims Dr. Ali. “The theory is that the more receptors it affects, the more effective the drug will be.”.

Sources indicate that the medication is currently in phase-three clinical trials, and it’s had some impressive results that suggest it could be the most effective drug for weight loss yet. The latest clinical trial results show that participants lost an average of 28.7% of their body weight on the highest dose of retatrutide over 68 weeks. By comparison, tirzepatide users lost an average of 15% to 22.5% over 72 weeks during clinical trials, and semaglutide users lost 10% to 15% of their body weight over 68 weeks during clinical trials.

It takes a little detective work, but there are some pharmacies that are selling the drug online.

Recent findings suggest that in fact, this has become such an matter that the FDA issued a press release in early February, stressing that it’s illegal to sell retatrutide (and fellow experimental weight loss medication cagrilintide) right now. That includes picking up the medication from a compounding pharmacy.

Sources indicate that “Retatrutide and cagrilintide cannot be used in compounding under federal law,” the release states. “Additionally, these are not components of FDA-approved drugs and have not been found safe and effective for any condition.”.

The FDA also noted that its officials have issued warning letters to companies that are distributing these medications.

This is hardly shocking, but doctors really want you to take a pass on using retatrutide before it’s FDA-approved.

“People should wait to take medications until they are approved by the FDA to maximize safety,” Richard Siegel, MD, codirector of the Diabetes and Lipid Center at Tufts Medical Center and endocrinologist at Tufts Medicine Weight & Wellness Center–Stoneham, tells SELF. “All scientific data in animals initially and then humans are carefully reviewed by the FDA for any signals that a medication may be harmful.”.

Sources indicate that that includes side effects you might experience now or in the future, Dr. Ali points out. Compounding pharmacies have become a gray area. They’re able to legally produce and sell their own versions of popular medications when the FDA-approved versions are in shortage. But technically this is no longer legal once the medications are out of shortage.

Recent findings suggest that but compounded drugs aren’t carefully regulated and may not even have the same ingredients or concentration as the medication they’re designed to mimic, Dr. Siegel states. “While these medications may be safe, there is less oversight in their production,” he says.

According to recent reports, dr. Ali warns against going directly through a compounding pharmacy, noting that it’s safer to work with your health care provider if you initiative to go this route. “The worst-case scenario is that you’re getting something unsafe or ineffective,” he says.

But, with all medications, Dr. Ali says it’s best to use the FDA-approved version whenever possible. “It’s going to work in a predictable way, and the side effect profile will be well-studied,” he says.

Dr. Siegel points out that there are a lot of options to lose weight right now. And, if you haven’t had success on one, he recommends talking to your healthcare provider about trying a different medication or strategy. If you haven’t had luck while working with a primary care physician, Dr. Ali suggests seeing an obesity medicine specialist who will be more knowledgeable about treatment options.

It has been revealed that “Medications for weight management are a powerful tool that should be used together with a comprehensive lifestyle strategy focusing on self-monitoring, optimal nutrition, and an exercise prescription, including both aerobic and resistance components,” Dr. Siegel says. Meaning, people who have the best results do more than take medication—they also focus on nutrition and exercise.

It has been revealed that if you’re interested in taking a weight loss medication or your existing treatment isn’t working, talk to a healthcare provider who specializes in this area. “These medications are designed for people with significant weight to lose,” Dr. Ali claims. “Most likely, they will need to be taken long-term.” That makes getting a well-vetted medication from a reputable source even more important, he points out.

Gentle manipulation and massage with your fingers can temporarily draw out the nipple.

Images courtesy of Ateliers Jean Nouvel.

French architecture studio Ateliers Jean Nouvel has shared photos revealing construction progress on the giant Shenzhen Opera House, due for completion in China in 2028.

Located on the Shekou Peninsula overlooking Shenzhen Bay, the opera house will eventually be defined by an elongated, wavy roofscape, nodding to the site’s connection to the sea.

Pritzker Prize-winning architect Jean Nouvel’s studio has designed it as a latest cultural landmark for the city, with a 2,300-seat concert hall, an 1,800-seat theatre and an 800-seat venue among its facilities.

The construction photos help visualise the scale of the 250,000-square-metre opera house, with its various facilities sprawling out across its waterfront site.

They showcase its main concert hall with its horseshoe-shaped plan, alongside the two smaller performance venues.

Ateliers Jean Nouvel’s design for Shenzhen Opera House was the winning entry of an invited international architecture competition, for which other entrants included MASSIVE, Snøhetta, MVRDV and Kengo Kuma.

Alongside the main performance halls, it will contain a multifunctional theatre with 400 seats, cultural spaces, backstage areas, apartments for performers and offices.

To help further connect the building to the surrounding water, the interior is expected to feature iridescent materials such as mother-of-pearl, also known as nacre.

“The sea will be both around you and over you,” explained Nouvel when the project was revealed in 2021.

“This explains more clearly why the main foyer has to be made of a noble, precious and luminous material that spells the meeting of sea and music and light,” Nouvel continued.

“Using the lustrous white reflections of a nacreous material will be a concrete poeticisation of the meeting of the sea and the auditorium and concert halls of the Opera House.”.

French architect Nouvel founded his eponymous studio in 1994. We recently reported on the news that the studio’s La Querola housing development in Andorra, designed with Spanish studio Ribas & Ribas Arquitectos, was damaged in a fire. The project won the housing category of this year’s Dezeen Awards, which took place last night.

Another landmark opera house recently featured on Dezeen is the Shanghai Grand Opera House, designed by Snøhetta with a giant spiral staircase.

Images courtesy of Ateliers Jean Nouvel.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.

Imagine stepping off a long-haul flight, exhausted and slightly rumpled, and walking into the Park Hyatt Tokyo — the hotel made iconic by *Lost in Translation* — and being handed a room key to a suite with floor-to-ceiling views of Mount Fuji. Or picture arriving at the Park Hyatt Paris-Vendôme, where Haussmann architecture frames your every view and the concierge greets you by name. Or standing in the Park Hyatt Newly introduced York, 25 floors above Midtown, watching the city sprawl in every direction from a room that costs more per night than most people's monthly car payment. Now imagine paying nearly nothing for it. That's the power of the World of Hyatt award chart — and the Park Hyatt sweet spot is one of the most emotionally resonant redemptions in all of travel rewards. Here's the math that makes the ChooseFI community's collective jaw drop: a single night at the Park Hyatt New York regularly retails for **$1,200–$2,000**. The Park Hyatt Tokyo commands **$800–$1,500** per night. The Park Hyatt Paris? Easily **$1,000+** in peak seasons. Yet every one of these properties sits at **Category 7**, bookable for just **25,000–30,000 World of Hyatt points** per night. At 30,000 points for a $1,500 room, you're extracting **5 cents per point (cpp)** — in a world where most loyalty programs are engineered to deliver 1–1.5 cpp if you're lucky. The CPP range for this sweet spot runs from **2.7 cpp all the way to 6.7 cpp**, meaning even a modest redemption delivers 2–3x the value of a typical points transaction. Why does this gap exist? Because Hyatt uses a **fixed award chart** anchored to categories, not real-time cash pricing. When demand spikes — New Year's Eve in New York, cherry blossom season in Tokyo, Paris Fashion Week — cash rates explode upward while your points cost stays locked. The hotel's revenue management team can't touch your award rate. That's the pricing inefficiency the ChooseFI community is built to exploit. This isn't aspirational travel for the ultra-wealthy. This is FI-minded travel: understanding the system, earning points intentionally, and converting them into experiences that would otherwise require an extra year of saving. A two-night stay at the Park Hyatt Tokyo for 60,000 points — points you can earn from a single credit card welcome bonus — is the kind of redemption that reframes what financial independence actually looks like in practice.

Skin in the Game: Is Adapalene or Salicylic Acid Better for Acne?

📅 31 Jul 2024 | ⏱️ 3 min read (629 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Greatist

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you have acne, you probably know more about skincare than most people.
  • But do you know what each treatment does for your skin and if one is better for acne?
  • Salicylic acid is a keratolytic agent commonly found in over-the-counter creams, face washes, masks, and gels.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you have acne, you probably know more about skincare than most people. You might even impress friends with terms like “adapalene” and “salicylic acid.”.

But do you know what each treatment does for your skin and if one is better for acne? Let’s find out!

Salicylic acid is a keratolytic agent commonly found in over-the-counter creams, face washes, masks, and gels. While it’s often used for acne, it can also help with dandruff, psoriasis, seborrheic dermatitis, calluses, and warts.

Adapalene, often known by its brand name Differin, is a topical retinoid. It comes in various forms, such as gels, cleansers, and creams. And just like salicylic acid, it’s available over-the-counter without a prescription.

On a chemical level, adapalene and salicylic acid work in different ways to clear acne.

Salicylic acid breaks down a protein called keratin in the outer layer of the skin. Studies show this helps remove the buildup of dead skin cells. It also reduces inflammation in the skin, calming the redness that often comes with breakouts.

Sources indicate that adapalene, on the other hand, is a retinoid. And what, you may ask, is a retinoid? It’s a derivative of vitamin A that attaches to receptors in the skin. Doing so prompts cell turnover to speed up, helping skin regenerate more quickly and lowering the likelihood of clogged pores.

So… what do these differences mean for acne? Both adapalene and salicylic acid can treat skin prone to breakouts (though it’s not recommended to use them together since this can over-irritate your skin).

In a recent development, which one is more potent may depend on your acne type. Research reveals that adapalene was among the best treatments for comedonal acne (aka whiteheads and blackheads), whereas salicylic acid was less effective and more affordable.

Long story short: Your dermatologist can help determine which is the smarter choice for your type of acne.

Studies haven’t directly compared adapalene and salicylic acid for blackheads, but both can help. Blackheads form from plugged hair follicles, and salicylic acid’s exfoliating action can clear clogged pores. Adapalene increases cell turnover, which can also help remove blackheads.

Adapalene is a retinoid. Retinoids are well-established anti-aging agents because they stimulate new cell growth and promote collagen production. Some studies have also shown anti-aging benefits from salicylic acid.

While salicylic acid, due to its exfoliating properties, can help reduce wrinkles, adapalene is generally more effective for addressing aging-related concerns like wrinkles.

It has been revealed that adapalene is an over-the-counter acne treatment — so prescription-strength options may work better. According to the American Academy of Dermatology, some of the most potent acne treatments include antibiotics and isotretinoin.

Recent findings suggest that adapalene isn’t a magic wand for acne. It may be an ideal choice for some people, but depending on your skin type and sensitivity level, salicylic acid, other OTC products, or even a prescription treatment might be your best bet.

Research shows that adapalene can be just as strong for zapping zits as benzoyl peroxide (another potentially powerful weapon in the battle against acne). A 2024 study, for example, found that 0.1% topical adapalene was as safe and effective as a 4% benzoyl peroxide solution in people of color.

Sources indicate that though adapalene may be an effective acne treatment, it’s not the pinnacle of retinoid strength. Of the four “generations” of retinoids, adapalene is considered third-generation. Fourth-generation retinoids are typically stronger and have higher specificity to retinoic acid receptors in the skin. For this reason, they’re available only by prescription.

Feel free to experiment with adapalene and salicylic acid to see which works best for you — after all, it’s your face! You might find one more effective for your skin. For expert advice, be sure to consult your dermatologist.
